item.title: GoodWe Marks 10 Years in India, Crosses 6 GW Inverter Shipments Milestone
item.description: Solar inverter manufacturer GoodWe recently marked 10 years of operations in India, celebrating a decade of growth in one of the world’s fastest-growing solar markets while announcing that its cumulative inverter shipments in the country have crossed 6 GW. The milestone was commemorated at an event held at The Lalit Ashok Bengaluru, where the company hosted customers, EPC partners, and industry stakeholders to reflect on its journey in India’s renewable energy sector. item.title: APTEL: Use of State Network for Solar Projects Attracts Transmission Charges
item.description: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) has ruled that solar projects using state transmission infrastructure are liable to pay applicable transmission charges, even if power evacuation involves the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS). The ruling came after a plea was filed by the Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd. item.title: NVVN To Solarise Campuses of Multiple AIIMS Campuses, Issues Tender
item.description: NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Ltd (NVVN), a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC Ltd, has invited bids from EPC companies to solarise three campuses of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) through rooftop solar systems. The project will involve installing 897 kW at AIIMS Deoghar, 858 kW at AIIMS Gorakhpur and 360 kW at AIIMS Patna. item.title: Ecofy Set To Raise Rs. 380 Cr Led By British International Investment
item.description: Ecofy Finance, a non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on renewable and clean tech solutions, is set to raise Rs 380 crore (approximately $43 million) in its Series B equity round led by British International Investment (BII). The company’s board has passed a special resolution to issue 20 equity shares and 38.05 crore Series B preference shares at a face value of Rs 10 each to raise Rs 380.5 crore, according to its regulatory filings sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). item.description: Solex Energy announced that its 3.78 gigawatt (GW) solar module manufacturing facility in Surat, Gujarat, has received approval under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy’s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) framework. item.title: NTPC Green Energy Adds 91.6 MW Solar Capacity, Expands Portfolio to 9.29 GW
item.description: NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) has announced the commercial operation of 91.6 megawatts (MW) of solar photovoltaic capacity in Andhra Pradesh, further strengthening the company’s expanding renewable energy portfolio. The declaration follows certification issued by the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) on March 9, 2026, confirming the project’s operational status. item.title: Enlight Metals Targets 1 GW Solar Structure Supply as It Expands Renewable Supply Chain
item.description: Enlight Metals, a technology-driven metal aggregation platform, is expanding its footprint in India’s solar supply chain, aiming to support around 1 GW of solar capacity with mounting structure materials over the next year, the company’s founders said in a recent interaction with Saur Energy. item.title: Arevon Energy Launches 430 MW Kelso Solar Project in Missouri
item.description: US-based renewable energy developer Arevon Energy has announced the commencement of operations at the 430 MWdc Kelso Solar Project located in Scott County, Missouri. Developed, constructed, and operated by Arevon, the project represents an investment of more than USD 500 million. The two-phase solar facility marks the company’s first utility-scale solar project in Missouri, significantly expanding the state’s clean energy capacity. item.description: Delhi-based Minda Corporation Limited (Minda Corp), the flagship company of Spark Minda, has entered into a joint venture (JV) agreement with Turntide Technologies (Turntide). item.description: ACME Solar Holdings said its subsidiary, ACME Eco Clean Energy Private Limited, has received a certificate of commissioning dated March 9, 2026 from the Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA) for a 4 MW portion of its 100 MW wind power project.
